payload.subject: Phase 1 module spec + one design fork: how phases line up across frames
payload.rationale: You told me to build Phase 1 fully parallel, no shared boundary, so I'm treating the Crystal Bravais wavetable as my own standalone artifact — not an export layer for the Torus work. Here's the plan in four pieces. First, a frame generator: for each of the seven Bravais crystal systems, synthesize one full cycle of that lattice's combined phonon partial spectrum. Second, frame interpolation: blend smoothly between those seven cycles into a 64- or 256-frame table you can sweep with one knob. Third, a writer that packs those frames into a valid Serum-format WAV. Fourth, a plain-WAV fallback for Ableton. One fork shapes the frame generator and I want to settle it before any code: how the cycles line up when you sweep. Reset each frame to a known starting point (clean sweeps, but it can flatten transient character), or carry the phase through (richer motion, risk of hollow comb-filter artifacts). I'm holding the Serum writer until a known-good reference WAV is confirmed on the Mac.

options.label: Reset every frame to the same starting point — predictable, clean sweeps; safest default
options.next: Frame generator emits each cycle phase-aligned to a fixed reference before interpolation.

options.label: Carry phase continuously across frames — richer motion, but risks comb-filter artifacts on the sweep
options.next: Frame generator preserves running phase; add an artifact listen-test before committing.

options.label: Reset now, expose carry-through as an option once the pipeline works end to end
options.next: Ship Phase 1 on zero-phase reset; defer continuous-phase to a later toggle.

payload.decision_topic: What is Stage 1 — the simplest possible Shepard tone?
payload.subject: Stage 1 scope: what counts as the simplest possible Shepard tone?
payload.rationale: My forward vector is staged revelation — Stage 1 is the simplest possible Shepard tone, and each later stage adds one physical or perceptual layer. The body of my home entry already describes a fairly rich architecture (monophonic portamento, all-octaves stack, per-voice key-tracked filters, global fixed Shepard bandpass). That is not Stage 1 — that is closer to Stage 4 or 5. Before I — or whoever ends up holding the synthesis code per `gsl-steward-020` — write anything, I want you to name what Stage 1 actually is, because the choice shapes every later stage. Three sketches I see. **MINIMUM-ILLUSION**: a static drone — one Shepard chord, no motion, no playability — just 7 octaves of one pitch class fading through a Gaussian envelope so the listener hears the characteristic Shepard timbre on its own. The illusion exists without motion. **MINIMUM-ASCENT**: an automated continuous glissando — same octave stack but the pitch class rises smoothly through a cycle so the listener hears the loop itself; no MIDI input, no portamento. The illusion as motion-without-arrival. **MINIMUM-PLAYABLE**: stripped-down monophonic instrument — discrete MIDI input, instant pitch jumps (no portamento yet), octave stack, fixed Shepard filter.
